payload.title: Automatically refresh public outputs after published content changes
payload.description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a publication editor, I want public outputs to refresh automatically whenever a saved change affects published content, so that readers and applications see consistent current publication state without a separate manual rebuild.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Automatically refresh public outputs after published content changes
  Scenario: Save a change to publicly published content
    Given an item has a publicly published version and public delivery channels are configured
    When I save a change that updates its publicly published content
    Then its public article representation and affected listings and indexes are automatically updated
    And the sitemap and both RSS and Atom feeds reflect the same selected published version and metadata
    And headless outputs are updated when enabled
    And stable item identity, canonical links and publication versus update timestamps remain consistent
  Scenario: Publish or unpublish an item
    Given an item can enter or leave public publication under the existing authorized lifecycle
    When it is published or unpublished
    Then the article, affected listings and indexes, sitemap, RSS and Atom consistently reflect its public eligibility within the documented freshness bound
    And enabled headless outputs reflect the same eligibility
    And delayed older work cannot restore withdrawn or superseded public content
  Scenario: Save a private draft
    Given an item is unpublished or has a private draft newer than its public version
    When I save changes only to the private draft
    Then no draft text, draft metadata or draft-only asset appears in any public article, listing, index, sitemap, feed or headless output
    And an existing published version remains the public source until an authorized public change occurs
  Scenario: An ancillary public projection fails
    Given an authorized content change has been saved but an affected ancillary output fails to refresh
    When the editor or operator inspects the outcome
    Then saved-content success and each known failed or pending public update are distinguishable
    And the failed update is visible and has a supported retry or reconciliation path
    And retry converges affected public outputs to current authorized published state without duplicate feed identities or revived withdrawn content
```

General Papyrus platform behavior, not a one-site sitemap audit. Both RSS and Atom are desired and share selection and metadata with the common foundation. Specify observable freshness, completion/failure reporting, retry/reconciliation and cache behavior before implementation. Orchestration, sequencing and atomicity remain design choices; do not prescribe a new service. Reuse/extend existing publish/save/unpublish and Markus/S3 incremental projection evidence (M3 PPY-3d905d) rather than invent a parallel publisher. Existing implementation evidence does not prove coverage of the new feed/headless outputs. RSS/Atom is the simplest first implementation candidate discussed; Monitoring may offer greater benefit, but neither implementation has been authorized.
